name: Alchemical Science
body:
Alchemical science is the traditional practice of many standard s-class investigators, and s-class investigators are just as likely to take it up to help themselves and, in some cases, allies in the heat of battle.

Basic Alchemy (Su)

When using Craft (alchemy) to create an alchemical item, an investigator gains a competence bonus equal to his class level on the Craft (alchemy) check. In addition, the investigator can use Craft (alchemy) to identify potions as if using detect magic. He must hold the potion for 1 round to make such a check.

Extracts (Sp)

An investigator with the alchemical science methodology creates extracts drawn from the alchemist formulae list. He must choose and prepare his extracts ahead of time.

An investigator can prepare an extract of any formula he knows. To learn or use an extract, the investigator must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the extract’s level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against the investigator’s extract is 10 + the extract level + the investigator’s Intelligence modifier.

An investigator can create only a certain number of extracts of each level per day. His base daily allotment of extracts is given on Table: S-Class Investigator. In addition, he receives bonus extracts per day if he has a high Intelligence score, in the same way a wizard receives bonus spells per day.

An investigator may know any number of formulae. Although the investigator doesn’t actually cast spells, he does have a formulae list that determines what extracts he can create. An investigator can utilize spell-trigger items if the spell appears on his formulae list, but not spell-completion items (unless he uses Use Magic Device to do so).

In many ways, extracts behave like spells in potion form, and as such their effects can be dispelled by effects like dispel magic using the investigator’s level as the caster level. Unlike potions, though, extracts can have powerful effects and duplicate spells that a potion normally could not.

Formula Books: An investigator stores his formulae in a special tome called a formula book. He must refer to this book whenever he prepares an extract but not when he consumes it.

Starting Formulae: The investigator begins play with two 1st-level formulae of his choice, plus a number of additional formulae equal to his Intelligence modifier. At each new investigator level, he gains one new formula of any level that he can create.

An investigator can also add formulae to his book just like a wizard adds spells to his spellbook, using the same costs and time requirements. He can study a wizard’s spellbook to learn any formula that is equivalent to a spell the spellbook contains. A wizard, however, cannot learn spells from a formula book. An investigator does not need to decipher arcane writings before copying them.

Creating and Using Extracts: Creating extracts consumes raw materials, but the cost of these materials is insignificant—comparable to the valueless material components of most spells. If a spell normally has a costly material component, that component is expended during the consumption of that particular extract. Extracts cannot be made from spells that have focus requirements (extracts that duplicate divine spells never have a divine focus requirement).

When the investigator mixes an extract, he infuses the chemicals and reagents in the extract with magic siphoned from his own magical aura. An extract immediately becomes inert if it leaves the investigator’s possession, reactivating as soon as it returns to his keeping—without the infusion alchemist discovery, an investigator cannot normally pass out his extracts for allies to use.

Once created, extracts remain potent for 1 day before becoming inert, so an investigator must re-prepare his extracts every day. Mixing an extract takes 1 minute of work—most investigators prepare many extracts at the start of the day or just before going on an adventure, but it’s not uncommon for one to keep some (or even all) of his daily extract slots open so that he can prepare extracts in the field as needed.

An extract is “cast” by drinking it, as if imbibing a potion—the effects of an extract exactly duplicate the spell upon which its formula is based, save that the spell always affects only the drinking investigator. The investigator uses his level as the caster level to determine any effect based on caster level.

Swift Alchemy (Ex)

At 3rd level, the investigator can create alchemical items with astounding speed. It takes an investigator half the normal amount of time to create alchemical items, and he can apply poison to a weapon as a move action.

Poison Immunity (Ex)

At 10th level, the investigator becomes completely immune to poison.
